I am 36 years old, and I have been working our land in Quzhou since I was a girl. I only went to primary school, so I do not read many books, but I know what our neighbors do and I follow what my mother and father taught me. My husband works part-time at a construction site in Handan, so most days I am the one who decides what to plant and spray. We have about ten mu of good flat land.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn—that is what everyone here does. I planted improved wheat seeds from the village supply store because they are cleaner than keeping my own seeds. This spring I will topdress with urea when the wheat turns green, and I will irrigate four times: at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling if the weather stays dry. I run the rotary tiller in the autumn before sowing, but I do not plough deep. I will spray pesticides about four times, mainly for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect around 1000 jin per mu, which is normal for our village. I do not buy straight phosphate or potash fertilizer—they are expensive and the compound fertilizer I spread at sowing already has a little.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant summer maize on the same seven mu. We do not till for maize anymore; we sow directly into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. I always buy hybrid maize seeds because the yield is much better than open-pollinated types. Maize does not need much extra nitrogen because the wheat fertilizer is still in the soil, but sometimes I put down a small handful of compound at planting. I will irrigate twice—once at the big trumpet leaf stage and once when the tassels emerge. Three sprays are enough to control corn borers and weeds. I expect about 1050 jin per mu.

I also keep two mu for cotton because the cotton price has been decent and I need cash for my daughter's school fees and for buying fertilizer. Cotton is backbreaking work—you have to spray medicine almost every week—but two mu is all I can manage by myself. I will rotary till the cotton field in early April and plant improved cotton seeds. I irrigate twice and spray about sixteen times to fight bollworms and aphids. If the weather cooperates I should get about 550 jin per mu of seed cotton.

I do not try new varieties I see on the internet. I buy what the seed seller at the market recommends and what my neighbors plant. That way, if something goes wrong, we all share the loss.
